paths.title: Learn Swift from zero
paths.summary: A language-first sequence: run a program, predict its values, construct types and verify a complete model before importing UI frameworks.
paths.audience: Start here even with extensive Kotlin or Java experience. Existing session IDs remain unchanged; the reading order starts at 057.
evidence: Run a scratch program and explain its output, including one failed prediction.
Implement collections, functions and value types without copying the answer.
Explain initialization, generic relationships, error propagation and captured lifetimes through actual calls.

stages.title: Run, express and transform
stages.summary: Learn syntax and collections before abstraction.

stages.title: Construct types and make contracts
stages.summary: Use initialization and generic companions after the corresponding type lesson, then attempt the integrated language lab. Async machinery belongs to the later production path.

stages.title: Revisit the original foundations
stages.summary: Apply the new language foundation to the current client and retrieval tasks.

paths.title: Learn SwiftUI from zero
paths.summary: Create a runnable app, compose controls, preview fixtures, share state and deliver a tested adaptive feature.
paths.audience: Complete the Swift bootcamp first, or demonstrate its language exercises. This path does not assume UIKit knowledge.
evidence: Build and run a synthetic app with the documented target and runtime.
Predict which identity owns each state value and verify updates and cancellation.
Deliver a feature with accessible controls, persistence, negative cases and independent review.

stages.title: First app to editable collections
stages.summary: Start with Xcode, controls and previews before observation and lists.

stages.title: Dependencies to a delivered feature
stages.summary: Build environment/style contracts, navigation, effects, adaptive UI and a persistent capstone.

paths.title: UIKit and mixed-framework delivery
paths.summary: Connect the beginner SwiftUI app to the UIKit/coordinator architecture used by the client.
paths.audience: After the language and SwiftUI tracks. Read legacy patterns accurately without assuming a repository-wide migration.
evidence: Trace one user action through public APIs and retained owners.
Build a reusable, keyboard-safe UI with all terminal flow outcomes.
Verify selection identity, bridge updates, large text and interrupted interaction.

stages.title: Controllers, bridges and feature evidence
stages.summary: Use the original delivery lessons with the runnable companion.

stages.title: UI engineering under change
stages.summary: Practice constraints, reusable lists, proposals, interaction, editing and scenes.

stages.title: UI runtime and scene correctness
stages.summary: Follow responder and runtime dispatch, inspect layer animation state, implement layout invalidation, and separate app, scene and view lifetimes.

paths.title: Production iOS engineering
paths.summary: Own concurrency, account-scoped data, performance, security, build artifacts and platform services with reproducible evidence.
paths.audience: After delivering one bounded scratch feature. A lesson may take multiple daily blocks; device-specific claims require device evidence.
evidence: Reject old success and error results under controlled schedules.
Retain a trace, explain a bottleneck and evaluate a correctness-preserving candidate.
Inspect the built artifact and exercise actual adapters separately from pure policy tests.

stages.title: Data and production contracts
stages.summary: Establish cancellation, storage, reliability, privacy and release boundaries.

stages.title: Measure the application and build
stages.summary: Record first investigations and turn observations into regression decisions.

stages.title: Own the dependency and artifact graph
stages.summary: Inspect configurations, resources, symbols, test execution and bounded changes.

stages.title: Connect platform capabilities
stages.summary: Wire system entry points and persistence before claiming platform competence.

stages.title: Event loops, scheduling and synchronization
stages.summary: Trace RunLoop delivery, compare legacy work ownership, protect short synchronous state, and avoid blocking a cooperative executor.

stages.title: Modern concurrency and language boundaries
stages.summary: Reproduce checking/settings differences, preserve transfer contracts, test clock/context/channel behavior, and identify unsafe ownership obligations.

stages.title: Durable data, offline replay and authentication
stages.summary: Upgrade actual old stores where supported, reload a persistent outbox, reconcile ambiguous writes, and keep account and protected-data ownership explicit.

stages.title: Instrument a workload and retain evidence
stages.summary: Build the instrumented scratch workload, capture real traces when a device is available, then analyze matching raw observations without inventing missing measurements.

stages.title: Deliver, review and sustain adoption
stages.summary: Inspect artifact identity and operational evidence, revise a staff delivery decision under critique, and defend a principal adoption or deprecation plan.

paths.title: Staff iOS engineering practice
paths.summary: Make sound decisions across feature boundaries: compare alternatives, own migration risk and improve the team's ability to deliver.
paths.audience: After repeated independently reviewed implementation. This is an evidence path, not a promotion checklist.
evidence: A reviewed RFC includes alternatives, compatibility, risk owners and a reversible rollout.
A measured improvement preserves correctness and has an operational owner.
Another engineer can reproduce the implementation and verification; adoption feedback changes the proposal.

stages.title: Bounded design and delivery
stages.summary: Connect data, architecture and cross-framework implementation.

stages.title: Evidence and operational accountability
stages.summary: Connect instrumentation, incident reasoning, privacy and delivery.

stages.title: Reviewed portfolio and influence
stages.summary: Submit artifacts and independent feedback, not attendance or self-scores.

stages.title: Verified delivery and independent revision
stages.summary: Connect durable recovery, actual diagnostic evidence and artifact identity to a challenged staff implementation handoff.

paths.title: Principal iOS platform practice
paths.summary: Practice multi-team platform strategy: product invariants, investment choices, compatibility portfolios, adoption and long-term operational accountability.
paths.audience: After sustained staff-level delivery and influence. The course provides review scenarios; principal competence requires real organizational outcomes.
evidence: A cross-team decision compares migration, coexistence and no-change options with explicit cost and risk.
A compatibility and ownership map covers consumers, SDK/OS constraints, account/process boundaries and recovery.
A staged adoption plan includes incentives, observability, deprecation exit criteria and evidence that can reverse the strategy.
Reviewers from affected teams challenge the proposal; revised decisions and sustained outcomes form the evidence.

stages.title: Platform boundaries and compatibility portfolio
stages.summary: Identify contracts across UI, services, modules, artifacts and extension processes.

stages.title: Investment, migration and operational risk
stages.summary: Use measured constraints rather than a framework preference.

stages.title: Multi-team review and sustained impact
stages.summary: Defend the worked strategy, revise it under critique and state missing organizational evidence.

stages.title: Runtime constraints and sustained platform outcomes
stages.summary: Test version/isolation and durable-transaction assumptions, then revise adoption and retirement decisions using independent evidence and exceptions.

paths.title: Runtime and production practice
paths.summary: Close the audited gaps through 24 sessions with concrete companions, explained assessment and separate host, native, device and review evidence.
paths.audience: After Swift, SwiftUI and the relevant core lessons; experienced Android engineers preparing to own iOS delivery.

stages.title: Event loops, scheduling and synchronization
stages.summary: Trace RunLoop delivery, compare legacy work ownership, protect short synchronous state, and avoid blocking a cooperative executor.

stages.title: Modern concurrency and language boundaries
stages.summary: Reproduce checking/settings differences, preserve transfer contracts, test clock/context/channel behavior, and identify unsafe ownership obligations.

stages.title: UI runtime and scene correctness
stages.summary: Follow responder and runtime dispatch, inspect layer animation state, implement layout invalidation, and separate app, scene and view lifetimes.

stages.title: Durable data, offline replay and authentication
stages.summary: Upgrade actual old stores where supported, reload a persistent outbox, reconcile ambiguous writes, and keep account and protected-data ownership explicit.

stages.title: Instrument a workload and retain evidence
stages.summary: Build the instrumented scratch workload, capture real traces when a device is available, then analyze matching raw observations without inventing missing measurements.

stages.title: Deliver, review and sustain adoption
stages.summary: Inspect artifact identity and operational evidence, revise a staff delivery decision under critique, and defend a principal adoption or deprecation plan.

evidence: A traced event or task lifetime and a reproduced correctness check, with effective language and isolation settings.
An old-store or durable-replay fixture plus explicit account, failure and recovery outcomes.
An actual trace or a clearly pending capture record, followed by a revised implementation and independent critique.

paths.title: Apple feature electives
paths.summary: Choose commerce, live updates, cloud documents, rich media or other Apple capabilities from product needs and platform contracts. These entry lessons do not establish mastery of every framework.
paths.audience: Engineers whose feature responsibility needs a specialist Apple capability after the core and production paths.

stages.title: Commerce and cloud lifetimes
stages.summary: Separate purchases and entitlements from UI updates, and durable local changes from multi-device conflict reconciliation.

stages.title: Media, text, hardware and additional platforms
stages.summary: Choose a bounded mechanism and measure its input, resource, lifecycle, entitlement and consent requirements.

evidence: A feature selection record explaining the required system contract and a viable simpler alternative.
A synthetic policy check or a bounded real sandbox/device exercise with environment and outcome recorded.
Explicit unsupported states, a recovery policy and the next specialist project or review owner.
